chunks: And from him, from Safwan, from al-'Iyyas ibn al-Qasim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the crescent moon when the people all see it and agree that it is for two nights, is that permissible? He said, 'Yes.'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْهِلَالِ: The crescent moon, used to mark the beginning of lunar months

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on communal agreement regarding the sighting of the moon for two nights?
ai.summary: This narration from Sahih al-Tusi highlights the principle of communal consensus (ittifaq) in lunar calendar determination, affirming that a unified sighting by the community is legally sufficient even if it implies the month begins on the 30th day (for two nights). It underscores the Shia jurisprudential reliance on observable evidence and collective agreement rather than strict astronomical calculation alone. This ruling is foundational for determining the start of Ramadan and Eid al-Fitr in Shia fiqh.
